title: Morse code translator
prompt:
Turn the words on the command line into Morse code. The starter already holds the code for every letter: 26 strings, and a table `morse` of 26 pointers to them in alphabet order, eight bytes each (`.dword`). The args box holds `hello world`. Change it to try other words with run. Check always uses `hello world`.

For each word from `argv[1]` on, walk its bytes with `ldrb` until the terminating zero. Turn each letter into a table index (`'a'` is 0, `'z'` is 25, and a capital counts the same as its lower-case letter), load the pointer at that index, and print the string it points to with `%s`. Anything that is not a letter prints `?`.

Spacing matters, because the output is compared exactly:

- one space between the letters of a word
- ` / ` between words
- a newline at the very end
- with no words at all, print `nothing to send` on its own line and return 1 from `main`

So `hello world` prints `.... . .-.. .-.. --- / .-- --- .-. .-.. -..`.

## what is checked

- the Morse line for `hello world`, the args in the specification, and for more arguments you cannot see
- the exit status (0 after a message, 1 with nothing to send)
- the words are read byte by byte (`ldrb`)
starter:
// send every command-line word as Morse code
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(nargs_r, w19)
define(args_r, x20)
define(i_r, w21)
define(ptr_r, x22)
define(first_r, w23)
define(table_r, x24)
define(ch_r, w25)

.data
m_a:        .string ".-"
m_b:        .string "-..."
m_c:        .string "-.-."
m_d:        .string "-.."
m_e:        .string "."
m_f:        .string "..-."
m_g:        .string "--."
m_h:        .string "...."
m_i:        .string ".."
m_j:        .string ".---"
m_k:        .string "-.-"
m_l:        .string ".-.."
m_m:        .string "--"
m_n:        .string "-."
m_o:        .string "---"
m_p:        .string ".--."
m_q:        .string "--.-"
m_r:        .string ".-."
m_s:        .string "..."
m_t:        .string "-"
m_u:        .string "..-"
m_v:        .string "...-"
m_w:        .string ".--"
m_x:        .string "-..-"
m_y:        .string "-.--"
m_z:        .string "--.."
unknown:    .string "?"

        .balign 8
morse:      .dword  m_a, m_b, m_c, m_d, m_e, m_f, m_g, m_h, m_i
            .dword  m_j, m_k, m_l, m_m, m_n, m_o, m_p, m_q, m_r
            .dword  m_s, m_t, m_u, m_v, m_w, m_x, m_y, m_z

fmt_code:   .string "%s"
fmt_gap:    .string " "
fmt_word:   .string " / "
fmt_end:    .string "\n"
fmt_none:   .string "nothing to send\n"

.text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        mov     nargs_r, w0
        mov     args_r, x1
        ldr     table_r, =morse

        // TODO: with no words on the command line, print fmt_none and
        // return 1. Otherwise, for each argv[i] from i = 1 up to argc - 1:
        //   - print fmt_word before every word except the first
        //   - walk its bytes up to the zero, printing fmt_gap before
        //     every letter except the word's first
        //   - turn the letter into an index (a is 0, z is 25, capitals
        //     count as lower case) and fetch its code from the morse
        //     table, whose entries are 8-byte pointers; anything that is
        //     not a letter prints unknown instead
        // End the line with fmt_end. printf wipes x0 to x18, so keep
        // everything you need afterwards in the aliased registers.

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
